nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph and $k$ a natural number. A labeling of the edges of $G$ with labels in $\{0, 1, \dots, k - 1\}$ is an arboricity coloring when, for each label $i$, the graph on the vertices of $G$ whose edges are the edges of $G$ labeled $i$ is acyclic, that is, a forest.
nodes.title: Arboricity colorings

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$ and let $k$ be a natural number. Then $G$ has an arboricity coloring with $k$ labels, that is, its edges can be labeled with $k$ labels so that the edges of each label form a forest, if and only if for every nonempty set $U \subseteq V$, the number of edges of $G$ with both endpoints in $U$ is at most $k(|U| - 1)$.
nodes.title: Nash–Williams arboricity theorem
